new_value: Landed the Rust pre-TX gate analysis and its landable slice (claimed): (1) TxError::NoKey added (-ENOKEY parity with lichen_link_tx.c:63-106) with Display string; (2) send_l2_payload_to — the single TX entry all production sends funnel through — documents the gate contract at the entry. KEY FINDING (changes the shape of the remaining work): the Rust link layer takes its signing identity as a MANDATORY constructor parameter (LinkLayer::new(identity)), so the C -ENOKEY unkeyed-context state is structurally unreachable in Rust — the has_key check is vacuous here. Likewise the C TDMA latch gate (-EBUSY when unsynced) has no Rust analog: Rust send paths carry Priority and are not slot-gated, and per the ehcn multicast-only decision DIO sends are re-targeted multicast. The genuinely missing Rust piece is a time/SFN-validity gate — which is exactly the wall-clock seam (bead nqtz-adjacent, b7z9.37.1.2(c-ii)). Rather than wiring a vacuous check, filed follow-up scoping: NoKey variant exists for API parity; the time/sync gate belongs to the wall-clock-seam slice. Tests: 337/337 green; fmt clean. The remaining oscore API residue edits in secure*.rs/tests were from the wall-clock bead's in-flight work — stashed (oscore-api-residue), not this bead's scope.
